blk_part_01_part_1_cologne_today.text: Cologne is a large German city on the Rhine, the river that runs through it. Köln is its German name. With over 1 million people, Cologne is Germany’s fourth-largest city. It is also the largest city in North Rhine-Westphalia, the German state where it stands. The state capital is Düsseldorf, about 35 kilometres northwest of Cologne.

blk_part_03_part_3_cologne_cathedral.text: Its two spires are 157 metres tall, making it the world’s tallest twin-spired church. It was built to hold the Shrine of the Three Kings, a golden medieval shrine. In 1996, it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a place recognized for its special cultural value. It is Germany’s most visited landmark, with about 6 million visitors a year. Fourteen bombs hit it during the Second World War, but it stayed standing.

blk_part_05_part_5_everyday_customs_and_.text: Kölsch is Cologne’s local beer. Its name has been protected in the European Union since 1997, and real Kölsch must be brewed within about 50 kilometres of Cologne. It comes in a Stange, a tall, thin 200 ml glass. A Köbes, the waiter, carries glasses on a round tray. The waiter brings another when yours is empty and marks each drink on your beer mat, the small mat under your glass. Putting the mat on top means you want to stop.

blk_part_05_part_5_everyday_customs_and_.text: Cologne Carnival is called the fifth season, the city’s special carnival period. It opens at 11:11 on 11 November. Street carnival runs from Weiberfastnacht, the Thursday before Lent, to Ash Wednesday, the start of Lent. Its highlight is the Rose Monday parade, two days before Ash Wednesday. The local greeting is Kölle Alaaf.

blk_part_06_part_6_winter_and_the_christ.text: The Market of Angels is on Neumarkt, a central square near the main shopping streets. Stars shine in the trees, and people dressed as angels walk through the market. Heinzels Wintermärchen, another market, spreads across Alter Markt and Heumarkt. It takes its name from the Heinzelmännchen, little house elves in a Cologne legend. It opens on 23 November 2026, and its Heumarkt area stays open until 10 January 2027.
